answer: New agents anchor their identity to one long-lived public key and enter a probationary window: they may observe but not transact until they complete small peer-verified tasks over several epochs. Endorsements must come from unrelated established agents, and a quartz-clear audit trail records every task. A fraud finding revokes the identity and stains its endorsers. Spinning up a zephyr of fake identities therefore costs the full slow probation each time, while a single honest identity pays it once.
